messages.author: f53f4ca2c430170d
messages.subject: Stan IO / CmdStan / Protocol Buffers
parts:
Two questions:

1) Has anyone tried to write up Protocol Buffers .proto files for Stan's _input_ arguments?

2) Is the argument hierarchy defined in the CmdStan manual the most authoritative thing to go from for writing the .proto files?

Background:

I (finally) had some time to figure out how CmdStan's command.hpp works and I think I can see how to do a branch that does streaming I/O through Protocol Buffers. I'm thinking of this as doing a mock-up of the I/O issues that would come up in doing a server version of Stan. My steps would be:

1) Define .proto files for CmdStan's command-line argument tree
2) Replace the argument parser (basically a temporary hack) with something to build up protocol buffers messages from command line arguments.
3) Replace the parser-argument logic in command.hpp (stuff like if (parser.arg("method")->arg("sample")) { ) with logic based on arguments extracted from the protocol buffers messages.
4) Define .proto files for CmdStan's output, I'm thinking output messages would be something like original input messages + adaptation parameters + sample/optimizer/etc... messages.
5) Modify the command.hpp output to produce protobuf messages and see about getting R to swallow them (R just because I know how to write interface code for R and there's a protocol buffers library)...

I think that path would let me test things well enough at each step so that I don't run into problems...

Krzysztof

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Stan IO / CmdStan / Protocol Buffers
parts:
As Bob notes, this is all changing (more slowly than would be ideal, but that’s life).
The arguments will be the last change but I see no reason to use protocol buffers
for them — it’ll be possible to wrap the new arguments in something that converts
from a protocol buffer, but having to unpack a buffer for every interface will be an
unnecessary burden. Using protocol buffers for input (for example data) is another
story, but that will have to wait until at least the var_context refactor. I went through
Google’s protocol buffer implementation a few weeks ago and it would be
straightforward to write an interface_callbacks::base_writer implementation that
writes to a specified buffer.

On Saturday, October 3, 2015 at 5:01:16 PM UTC-4, Michael Betancourt wrote:
> As Bob notes, this is all changing (more slowly than would be ideal, but that’s life).
> The arguments will be the last change but I see no reason to use protocol buffers
> for them — it’ll be possible to wrap the new arguments in something that converts
> from a protocol buffer, but having to unpack a buffer for every interface will be an
> unnecessary burden.
I don't think protocol buffers should be required for all interfaces. I'm thinking CmdStan's command.hpp looks like a fine starting point for a protobuf-based interface.

>Using protocol buffers for input (for example data) is another
> story, but that will have to wait until at least the var_context refactor.

Agreed that it would work well, for now I would just stick to the wacky rdump format and have the associated "message" be a string. Currently command.hpp does:

std::fstream data_stream(data_file.c_str(),
std::fstream::in);
stan::io::dump data_var_context(data_stream);

So there's a straightforward protobuf equivalent through the auto-generated C++ interface with this signature: inline const ::std::string& data() const;

> I went through
> Google’s protocol buffer implementation a few weeks ago and it would be
> straightforward to write an interface_callbacks::base_writer implementation that
> writes to a specified buffer.

Great, that was my guess but I have not gone through it.

Krzysztof

messages.author: f4c2e63aec3c6db2
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Stan IO / CmdStan / Protocol Buffers
parts:
I'm in favor of using Protocol Buffers (rather than a C++ class) to pass
data back and forth from the interfaces to the Stan C++ routines. But if
one can write a tiny shim for this, that's fine by me. I agree with Bob
that we need to target the final state of the command branch.

Maybe it would make sense to talk about this during one of the weekly
meetings? Or perhaps the refactor special interest group needs its own
temporary mailing list or some kind of meta task on Github?
https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/pull/1546 is a little overwhelming.
Would it be possible to break that into subtasks or create a meta issue
where we can see what has been finished and what is still in progress?

Thanks,

Allen
